metaDescription: Explore the science behind everyday objects.
footerTagline: The science of everyday objects, from what you can see to why it works. Every lesson says where it comes from.
footerLegal: © {year} Science Behind It. Lessons explain science; they are not professional advice.
homeLead: Point your camera at an everyday object, or describe it. You get a real problem to solve, watch it worked out, then try it yourself by changing a live experiment.
homePhotoPrivacy: Photos are only used to recognise the object and are deleted within {days} days.
exampleProblemStart: The print on a medicine bottle is too small to read.
exampleProblemMarked: Where do you hold the glass
exampleGuessText: Close to the print, or far above it?
exampleTryText: Move the lens in the experiment and watch the magnification change until the print is big enough.
howShowText: Take a photo or type what it is. We name what we see and start your lesson; if we get it wrong, you can say what it is.
howProblemText: A real task with your object, and a guess before anything is explained.
howWatchText: See the answer worked out, then change the experiment yourself to solve new challenges.
insideIntro: The same five steps, in the same order, so you always know where you are.
moduleBlurbProblem: A real task with your object, to start from.
moduleBlurbActivate: Links it to what you already know, then you make a guess.
moduleBlurbDemonstrate: The answer worked out step by step, in a live experiment.
moduleBlurbApply: Solve new challenges yourself by changing the experiment.
moduleBlurbIntegrate: Something to notice or try in your own day.
trustHeading: Built so you can trust it
trustSourcesText: Lessons draw on open textbooks and public science institutions, and every lesson lists the sources it used.
trustCheckedText: Each sourced statement is checked against the passage it comes from before it can appear in a lesson.
trustGapsText: Where no trusted source covers a point, the AI fills it from general knowledge and the lesson says so at the top.
trustSafetyText: Lessons about medicines, chemicals, electricity and wild mushrooms start with a safety note and stay with the ideas.
forIntro: Choose how deep to go. You can also set an age band, Child, Teen or Adult, if you want; we never guess your age.
depthQuickText: Short, simple words for a first look while the object is in your hand.
depthExploreText: An everyday explanation that builds the answer one step at a time.
depthDeeperText: More technical detail, with the sources to follow up.
ctaText: Pick one near you and find out how it works.
aboutLead: A way to understand how everyday things work, starting from what you can see.
aboutMadeShow: You show us an object, or type what it is, and we start a lesson about it.
aboutMadeSearch: We break your question into smaller ones and look for answers in open textbooks and public science institutions.
aboutMadeCheck: Each statement is checked against the passage it comes from before it can appear in a lesson, and every lesson lists its sources.
aboutMadeGaps: Where no trusted source is found, the AI fills the gap from its general knowledge, and the lesson says so at the top.
aboutMadeReviewer: Lessons that have not been checked by a reviewer say that too.
aboutNotText: Lessons explain the science behind an object. They are not advice on using, repairing, eating or taking anything. Lessons about medicines, chemicals, electricity and wild mushrooms start with a safety note and stay with the ideas.
aboutReportText: Every lesson ends with a way to report a problem. Reports go to a reviewer with the exact version of the lesson you read.
privacyLead: What happens to your photo, your question and your feedback, in plain words.
privacyPhotoUse: We use it only to recognise the object for your lesson.
privacyPhotoStrip: Before upload, your device removes location and camera details from the photo, and we remove them again when it arrives.
privacyPhotoStorage: It is stored privately on Cloudflare R2 and never shown to other learners. When photo recognition is on, it is sent to Meta's model API, or to OpenAI's if Meta is unavailable; neither may train on it.
privacyPhotoRetention: It is deleted within {days} days, or sooner once recognised, unless you choose to keep it. A kept photo stays until you delete it, below.
privacyQuestionSent: Your question and what the lesson is about (the name we recognised or the words you typed) are sent to the AI model that writes your lesson. The lesson is stored with its sources and checks so a reviewer can look at it; your photo is never part of a lesson.
privacyQuestionSettings: Your choice of depth and age band stays in this browser tab and is only used to ask for the right version of a lesson. We never guess your age.
privacyFeedbackStored: Ratings and problem reports are stored with the lesson they are about, not with you.
privacyFeedbackRetention: Anything you type in a report is deleted after 90 days. Please leave out your name and other personal details.
privacyAccountOptional: Accounts are optional and for people 13 and over. Every lesson works without one.
privacyAccountKept: We keep your name, email, the age you gave when signing up, and a scrambled form of your password that cannot be turned back into it. If you sign in with Google, Google tells us your name and email; we never see your Google password.
privacyAccountEmails: Emails to confirm your address or reset your password are sent through ZeptoMail. They hold only the link.
privacyAccountCookie: Signing in sets one cookie that keeps you signed in for 30 days, or until you sign out.
privacyAccountSaving: Saving a lesson keeps which lesson and version you saved, so only you can open it again. It never keeps your photo; that is always its own choice.
privacyAccountLinking: Linking this device to your account is a separate choice, made on your account page.
privacyAccountExport: On your account page you can download everything tied to your account, or delete it all at once. Deletion is immediate, and copies in our backups are gone within 30 days.
privacyFontsText: Fonts are served by us, so reading a lesson does not contact a font company. Links to sources open the source's own site, which has its own privacy rules.
choicesIntro: Each choice is separate and starts off. We only ask for one when there is something it would do, and you can change your mind here at any time.
choicesKeepingOn: You chose to keep photos. They stay in private storage until you delete them.
choicesStopKeeping: Stop keeping photos and delete them
choicesKeepingOff: Off. Photos are deleted about an hour after we recognise them. You can choose to keep one after it is recognised.
choicesLinkingOn: On. This device's kept photos are tied to your account.
choicesLinkingOff: Off. Accounts are optional, and linking is a separate choice.
choicesLinkingChange: Change this on your account page
